title: Production, Characterization and Potential Uses of a 3D Tissue-engineered Human Esophageal Mucosal Model
protocol: Prepare epithelial culture medium by mixing DMEM and Ham's F12 in a 3:1 ratio (v:v).

Add 10% (v/v) fetal calf serum, 10 ng/ml epidermal growth factor, 0.4 μg/ml hydrocortisone, 1.8 x 10-4 M adenine, 5 μg/ml insulin, 5 μg/ml transferrin, 2 x 10-7 M triiodothyronine, 1 x 10-10 M cholera toxin, 2 x 10-3 M glutamine, 100 IU/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, and 0.625 μg/ml amphotericin B to the medium.
Put 11 ml of DMEM, 10% fetal calf serum, 2 x 10-3 M L-glutamine, 100 IU/ml penicillin, 100 μg/ml streptomycin, and 0.625 μg/ml amphotericin B into a T75 tissue culture flask.
Add 1 ml of the same medium containing 1 x 10^6 lethally irradiated mouse 3T3 fibroblasts to produce a feeder layer for epithelial cells.
Incubate overnight at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
Dissect an approximately 2 cm² sample of disease-free background esophageal squamous mucosa tissue from patients undergoing surgery using a scalpel.
Transport the tissue in a 50 ml container with sterile transport medium at room temperature.
Store the tissue in the transport medium for up to 12 hours (overnight) at 4 °C, but do not exceed this storage period as it affects cell viability.
Sterilize a scalpel blade by soaking it in 70% ethanol for 5 minutes.
Rinse the sterilized scalpel blade with sterile PBS.
Place the tissue sample in a sterile Petri dish and cut it into 0.5 cm strips using the scalpel.
Add 5 ml of 0.1% (w/v) trypsin in PBS to the Petri dish containing the tissue strips, cover the dish with its lid, and incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour.
After the incubation period, add 5 ml of fetal calf serum (FCS) to the Petri dish to inhibit the action of the trypsin.
Use sterile forceps to hold a tissue strip and gently scrape the epithelial surface with the scalpel blade for 1-2 minutes per strip to remove epithelial cells into the medium.
Remove the scraped tissue from the medium and set it aside.
Repeat the scraping process for all remaining tissue strips.
Collect the medium containing the detached epithelial cells into a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 200 x g for 5 minutes.
Pour off the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 12 ml of epithelial medium.
Discard the medium from the feeder cell layer in the T75 flask.
Add the cell suspension containing freshly isolated epithelial cells to the flask.
Incubate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere for 24 hours.
Pour off and discard the culture medium after 24 hours.
Replace with 12 ml of fresh epithelial medium.
Continue incubating at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
View colonies under a standard light microscope as they appear over the next 24 to 48 hours.
Pour off and replace spent culture medium every 2 to 3 days with an equal volume of fresh medium.
Once the flask reaches 80% confluency, passage the cells in a ratio of 1:5.
Establish feeder layers of irradiated 3T3 cells in each flask prior to passaging the cells.
Work in a laminar flow cabinet using sterile technique.
Place the tissue in a sterile Petri dish and mince finely with a sterile scalpel blade.
Add 10 ml of 0.5% (w/v) collagenase A solution to the minced tissue.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
Transfer the digest to a 15 ml centrifuge tube and centrifuge for 10 min at 200 x g.

Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 ml of fibroblast culture medium (DMEM 10% FCS, 2 x 10-3 M L-glutamine, 100 IU/ml penicillin, 100 µg/ml streptomycin, and 0.625 µg/ml amphotericin B).
Place the suspension into a T75 flask and incubate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
After 24 hours, pour off the medium containing debris and replace with 12 ml of fresh fibroblast medium.
Replace the culture medium every 2 to 3 days.
Passage cells once they reach 80% confluency by splitting them in a 1:5 ratio.
Use fibroblast cells between passages 4 and 10 for the model described below.
Place the freshly excised esophagus into a sterile pot containing approximately 150 ml of 10% povidone-iodine solution for 5 min.
Transfer the esophagus to a second pot containing approximately 100 ml of sterile PBS with penicillin, streptomycin, and amphotericin B.
Transport the container at room temperature back to the laboratory.
Sterilize tweezers, scissors, and scalpel blades by soaking in 70% ethanol for 5 min and rinsing in sterile PBS.
Handle the esophagus using sterile tweezers.
Cut open the esophagus longitudinally with scissors.
Rinse the tissue by placing the esophagus into a pot containing approximately 100 ml of sterile PBS and shaking gently to remove debris.
Clean a cork dissection board by spraying liberally with 70% ethanol and allowing it to dry.
Remove the esophagus from the PBS.
Pin out the esophagus onto the board, mucosal surface uppermost.
Grasp the mucosal surface at one end with sterile tweezers and pull away from the board to separate it from the submucosa.
Use a sterile scalpel blade to dissect the esophagus longitudinally along the lamina propria, removing pins as dissection progresses.
Discard the most proximal and distal 2 cm of the mucosa.
Cut the remaining tissue into pieces measuring approximately 5 cm².
Place all cut tissue into a 180 ml sterile pot containing approximately 150 ml of sterile PBS.
Agitate gently to rinse the tissue.
Using sterile tweezers, transfer the cut tissue into a 180 ml pot containing 150 ml of sterile 1 M NaCl, 200 IU/ml penicillin, 200 µg/ml streptomycin and 1.25 µg/ml amphotericin B.
Incubate for 72 hr at 37 °C.
Place the tissue into a fresh 180 ml pot containing 150 ml sterile PBS.
Gently peel the detaching epithelium from the pig esophagus using sterile forceps and discard.
Place the remaining tissue into a fresh 180 ml pot and add 150 ml of sterile PBS.
Agitate gently for 5 min to wash.
Pour off the PBS and repeat with fresh PBS two more times.
Place all the tissue into a 500 ml glass bottle containing 400 ml of sterile 80% (v/v) glycerol solution for 24 hr at room temperature.
Transfer to 400 ml of sterile 90% (v/v) glycerol solution for a further 24 hr.
Store in 400 ml of sterile 100% glycerol solution at room temperature for a minimum of 4 months.
Allow the bottle to cool and the Chelex to settle.
Pour off excess water in a laminar flow cabinet.
Add 500 ml of newborn calf serum (NCS) and stir overnight at 4 °C.
Stop stirring and allow the Chelex to settle.
Decant chelated serum using a sterile pipette without disturbing the Chelex.
Store decanted serum in 10 ml aliquots at -20 °C.

Prepare Composite Medium I by mixing DMEM and Hams F12 (3:1 ratio), adding L-glutamine, hydrocortisone, O-phosphorylethanolamine, triiodothyronine, adenine, CaCl2, progesterone, insulin, transferrin, selenium, ethanolamine, and 0.1% chelated NCS.
Prepare Composite Medium II by replacing chelated serum with 0.1% non-chelated NCS in the recipe for Composite Medium I.
Prepare Composite Medium III by omitting progesterone and increasing serum to 2% non-chelated NCS in the recipe for Composite Medium II.
Perform all work in a laminar flow hood using aseptic technique.
Sterilize tools by soaking in 70% ethanol for 5 min, then rinsing with sterile PBS.
Rehydrate the acellular porcine esophageal scaffold in sterile PBS.
Agitate and soak the tissue for 10 minutes.
Decant the PBS and replace with fresh PBS.
Repeat washing process five times to remove glycerol traces.
Incubate rehydrated tissue overnight in DMEM at 37 °C.
Place a 5 cm² acellular scaffold into a 6 well plate, submucosal side uppermost.
Position a sterile medical grade stainless steel ring onto the center of each scaffold and press down to ensure an adequate seal with the tissue.
Harvest fibroblasts using Trypsin-EDTA.
Count cells using a haemocytometer.
Centrifuge cell suspension for 10 minutes at 200 x g.
Resuspend cell pellet into fibroblast medium to produce a final cell count of 2.5 x 10⁶ cells per ml.
Add 0.2 ml of fibroblast medium containing 5 x 10^5 human esophageal fibroblasts within each ring.
Flood the area around the outside of the ring with approximately 2 ml of fibroblast medium.
Incubate at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
Remove the rings and fibroblast medium after 24 hours.
Add at least 5 ml of fresh fibroblast medium to each well to ensure the scaffold is totally immersed.
Culture for 1 week, replacing the medium every 2 to 3 days.
Remove the 6-well plates containing the scaffolds to a laminar flow hood after 1 week.
Invert each scaffold using sterile forceps, placing the mucosal surface uppermost.
Place steel rings on the mucosal surface in the center of the tissue.
Add 2 ml of sterile 0.02% (w/v) EDTA solution to each T75 flask for epithelial cells after PBS wash.
Incubate for 2 minutes at 37 °C.
Tap the flask gently to detach the i3T3 feeder layer while leaving the epithelial cells attached.
Pour off the EDTA solution containing the feeder layer.
Add trypsin-EDTA solution to harvest the epithelial cells.
Count the harvested cells using a haemocytometer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 10 minutes at 200 x g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in Composite Medium 1 to achieve a final concentration of 5 x 10^6 cells per ml.
Add 0.2 ml of Composite Medium I containing 1 x 10^6 epithelial cells within the ring.
Flood the area around the outside of the ring with approximately 2 ml of Composite Medium I.
Place the constructs into the incubator at 37 °C in a 5% CO2, humidified atmosphere.
After 24 hours (Day 1), remove the rings and medium.
Add at least 5 ml of fresh Composite Medium I to ensure scaffolds are fully submerged.
Return the constructs to the incubator.
After another 24 hours (Day 2), remove the medium.
Replace with at least 5 ml of Composite Medium II, ensuring scaffolds are fully submerged.
Return the constructs to the incubator.
Place sterile medical grade stainless steel mesh grids into fresh 6 well plates, one per construct.
Transfer constructs onto the top of the steel grids using sterile tweezers, mucosal surface uppermost.
Add sufficient Composite Medium III so that the liquid reaches the underside of the composite but does not cover the surface.
Maintain composites at an air-liquid interface for between 10 and 20 days.
Replace Composite Medium III with fresh medium every 2 to 3 days.
Fix constructs for histological analysis and immunohistochemical staining after the experiment.
Extract protein from the epithelium for further analysis after the experiment.
Extract RNA from the epithelium for further analysis after the experiment.
Retain conditioned culture medium for analysis of extracellular signaling molecules if required.
